definition_zh: 游泳；游动；浸在液体中；眩晕
definition_en: to move through water using the body, or to seem to spin around
core_image: 孩子在水面划开双臂，身体贴着水线前进
scene: 夏天他们去河里游泳。In summer they swim in the river.
sceneCN: 这里 swim 是「游泳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夏天他们去河里游泳。

senses.title: To move through water
senses.definition: to move through water by moving the arms and legs
senses.definitionCN: 靠划动四肢在水中前进
senses.example: In summer they swim in the river.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天他们去河里游泳。
senses.why: This is the physical action the word first named.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最早命名的身体动作。

senses.title: To be covered in liquid
senses.definition: to be covered with or full of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 被液体覆盖或充满
senses.example: The vegetables were swimming in oil.
senses.exampleCN: 蔬菜浸在油里。
senses.why: The image of moving in water is transferred to food sitting in sauce.
senses.whyCN: 在水中移动的画面被移用到泡在汤汁里的食物上。

senses.title: To feel dizzy
senses.definition: to seem to go round and round
senses.definitionCN: 感觉一切在旋转
senses.example: The room began to swim before his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 房间开始在他眼前旋转。
senses.why: A swimmer loses steady footing, so the word also names the unstable feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 游泳者失去稳定立足点，于是这个词也用来命名那种不稳的感觉。

senses.title: The activity of swimming
senses.definition: the act or sport of moving through water
senses.definitionCN: 在水中前进的活动或运动
senses.example: She had a long swim before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 早饭前她游了很久。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the whole activity, as English often does.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，指整个活动，这在英语里很常见。

intro.en: Swim comes from an old Germanic verb for moving through water.

items.en: The Germanic root carried the idea of moving through water.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根带有在水中行进的含义。

items.en: Swimman meant to swim.

items.en: Swim also described things covered in liquid.

items.en: Swim gained the sense of a dizzy, spinning feeling.

abstract.en: A swim is a small journey with no road.

definition_zh: 摇摆；摆动；转身；秋千；转变
definition_en: to move back and forth, or a seat hanging on ropes
core_image: 孩子在秋千上前后荡起，绳子划出弧线
scene: 孩子用力荡着秋千。The child pushed the swing high into the air.
sceneCN: 这里 swing 是「秋千」（第 3 个义项）；句意：孩子把秋千推得很高。

senses.title: To move back and forth
senses.definition: to move backwards and forwards from a fixed point
senses.definitionCN: 从固定点来回移动
senses.example: The lamp swung in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 灯在风中摇摆。
senses.why: The hanging seat gave the word its basic picture of motion around a pivot.
senses.whyCN: 悬挂的座位给这个词提供了绕支点运动的基本画面。

senses.title: To turn sharply
senses.definition: to turn quickly in a particular direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝某方向迅速转动
senses.example: She swung round to face him.
senses.exampleCN: 她转身面对他。
senses.why: A swinging object changes direction, so a person turning quickly is described the same way.
senses.whyCN: 摆动的物体改变方向，于是迅速转身的人也用同样的说法。

senses.title: A seat on ropes
senses.definition: a seat hanging from ropes that a person rides for fun
senses.definitionCN: 用绳索吊起供人玩耍的座位
senses.example: The children queued for the swing.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们排队等秋千。
senses.why: The noun names the very object whose motion produced the verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的正是产生这个动词的那种物体。

senses.title: A shift in opinion
senses.definition: a change from one position or opinion to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种立场或观点转向另一种
senses.example: There was a swing towards the opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 出现了倒向反对派的转变。
senses.why: A pendulum moves to the other side, so a change of opinion is pictured as a swing.
senses.whyCN: 钟摆摆向另一边，于是观点的改变被画成一次摆动。

intro.en: Swing comes from an old Germanic verb for beating or swinging.
intro.cn: swing 源自古老的日耳曼语动词，意为挥打或摆动。

items.en: The root described a sweeping, swinging movement.
items.cn: 该词根描述挥扫、摆动的动作。

items.en: Swingan meant to beat or flog.
items.cn: swingan 意为击打或鞭打。

items.en: Swingen widened to any back and forth motion.
items.cn: swingen 扩展到任何来回运动。

items.en: Swing named the hanging seat children ride.
items.cn: swing 指孩子们玩的悬挂座位。

items.en: Swing extended to shifts of opinion and mood.
items.cn: swing 又扩展到观点与情绪的变化。

note.en: Swing is compared with look-alike words and with words for moving to and fro.
note.cn: 把 swing 与形近词以及表示来回移动的词作比较。

to move slowly from side to side
to move gently back and forth

normalIntro.en: Swing is motion around a hanging point, then any shift to the other side.

normal.en: The lamp swung in the wind.
She swung round to face him.
The children queued for the swing.
There was a swing towards the opposition.
normal.cn: 出现了倒向反对派的转变。

normal.en: He swung the bag onto his shoulder.

abstract.en: A swing is a promise that what goes up comes back.

abstract.en: Opinion swings like a pendulum, never resting long.

abstract.en: To swing is to give your weight to something outside you.
abstract.cn: 荡秋千就是把重量交给身外之物。

examples.en: The lamp swung in the wind.
The children queued for the swing.
There was a swing towards the opposition.
examples.cn: 出现了倒向反对派的转变。

dict_mnemonic.note: 不规则变化 · swing - swung - swung

root: 来自古英语 swingan（挥打），源于日耳曼语，核心是绕支点的挥摆动作。

sensesIntro.en: Swing covers back and forth motion, a hanging seat, and a shift to another side.
sensesIntro.cn: swing 涵盖来回摆动、悬挂座椅以及转向另一边的变化。

core.en: Motion around a fixed point, always returning.
core.cn: 绕固定点运动，总会返回。

branches.en: The lamp swung in the wind.

items.meaning: to move from side to side

latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂。

definition_en: a device that turns power on or off, or a change from one thing to another
core_image: 手指按下墙上的开关，房间立刻亮起
scene: 她按下开关，灯亮了。She pressed the switch and the light came on.
sceneCN: 这里 switch 是「开关」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她按下开关，灯亮了。

senses.title: A device for turning power on and off
senses.definition: a small device that starts or stops an electric current
senses.definitionCN: 启动或切断电流的小装置
senses.example: She pressed the switch and the light came on.
senses.exampleCN: 她按下开关，灯亮了。
senses.why: The word first named a thin twig, and a twig flicked to make contact gave the electric device its name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指细树枝，用树枝轻弹接通电路的装置因此得名。

senses.title: To change to something else
senses.definition: to change from one thing or system to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一种事物或系统改为另一种
senses.example: We switched to a cheaper supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 我们换成了更便宜的供应商。
senses.why: Flicking a switch changes the state at once, so any quick change is called a switch.
senses.whyCN: 拨动开关立刻改变状态，于是任何快速改变都叫 switch。

senses.title: A change or exchange
senses.definition: an act of changing from one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一事物转为另一事物的行为
senses.example: There has been a switch in policy.
senses.exampleCN: 政策出现了转变。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the change itself, as often happens in English.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词指这种改变本身，这在英语里很常见。

senses.title: To exchange one for another
senses.definition: to exchange the positions of two things
senses.definitionCN: 互换两个事物的位置
senses.example: They switched seats before the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影开场前他们换了座位。
senses.why: Two poles of a switch swap contact, so swapping places is a natural extension.
senses.whyCN: 开关的两极交换接触，因此互换位置是自然引申。

intro.en: Switch began as the name of a thin, flexible twig.

items.en: A related Germanic word named a thin twig or whip.

items.en: Switche meant a slender riding whip.
items.cn: switche 意为细长的马鞭。

items.en: Switch named a device that makes or breaks contact.
items.cn: switch 指接通或断开接触的装置。

items.en: Switch became a verb meaning to change over.
items.cn: switch 成为动词，表示转换。

items.en: Switch extended to swapping places or roles.
items.cn: switch 又扩展到互换位置或角色。

note.en: Switch is compared with look-alike words and with words for changing.
note.cn: 把 switch 与形近词以及表示改变的词作比较。

definition_en: enlarged because of injury, liquid, or pressure
core_image: 扭伤的脚踝鼓起来，皮肤绷得发亮
scene: 他扭伤后脚踝肿了。His ankle was swollen after the fall.
sceneCN: 这里 swollen 是「肿胀的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：摔倒后他的脚踝肿了。

senses.title: Enlarged by injury or liquid
senses.definition: larger than normal because of fluid or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因液体或受伤而比正常更大
senses.example: His ankle was swollen after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒后他的脚踝肿了。
senses.why: The past participle of swell keeps the picture of something filling and rising.
senses.whyCN: swell 的过去分词保留了某物被填满并隆起的画面。

senses.title: Increased in size or amount
senses.definition: made larger in size or number
senses.definitionCN: 在体积或数量上变大
senses.example: The swollen budget worried the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 膨胀的预算让委员会担忧。
senses.why: What fills with liquid can also fill with numbers, so size itself can be swollen.
senses.whyCN: 能充满液体的也能充满数字，因此规模本身也可以「膨胀」。

senses.title: Rising above its banks
senses.definition: having more water than usual, as a river
senses.definitionCN: 水位高于平常的，如河流
senses.example: The swollen river swept away the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 涨水的河流冲走了桥。
senses.why: A river that swells rises like injured flesh, so the same word describes both.
senses.whyCN: 上涨的河像肿起的皮肉一样隆起，于是同一个词兼指两者。

items.en: The root meant to grow or become big.

items.en: Swollen extended to rivers, budgets and pride.

note.en: Swollen is compared with look-alike words and with words for being enlarged.

definition_en: a sign that shows an illness or a deeper problem
core_image: 体温计上的水银升到红色刻度，医生记下这笔
scene: 发烧是感染的常见症状。Fever is a common symptom of infection.
sceneCN: 这里 symptom 是「症状」（第 1 个义项）；句意：发烧是感染的常见症状。

senses.title: A sign of illness
senses.definition: a change in the body that shows a disease
senses.definitionCN: 显示疾病的身体变化
senses.example: Fever is a common symptom of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧是感染的常见症状。
senses.why: The Greek word meant a chance happening that falls together with something else.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词意为与某事同时发生的偶然现象。

senses.title: A sign of a wider problem
senses.definition: a sign that something else is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 表明其他方面出了问题的迹象
senses.example: Rising debt is a symptom of deeper trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 债务上升是更深层问题的征兆。
senses.why: If a bodily sign can point to a disease, any sign can point to a hidden cause.
senses.whyCN: 身体迹象可以指向疾病，任何迹象也就能指向隐藏的根源。

intro.en: Symptom comes from Greek symptoma, something that falls together.
intro.cn: symptom 源自希腊语 symptoma，意为同时发生之事。

items.en: Symptoma meant a chance event falling with another.
items.cn: symptoma 意为与另一事同时发生的偶然事件。

items.en: Piptein meant to fall.
items.cn: piptein 意为落下。

items.en: Symptoma became a medical term for a sign of disease.
items.cn: symptoma 成为指疾病迹象的医学术语。

items.en: French symptome carried the medical sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 symptome 把医学含义带入英语。

items.en: Symptom widened to signs of any deeper problem.
items.cn: symptom 扩展到任何深层问题的迹象。

note.en: Symptom is compared with look-alike words and with other signs.
note.cn: 把 symptom 与形近词以及其他表示迹象的词作比较。

normalIntro.cn: symptom 是指向隐藏原因的外在迹象。

normal.cn: 发烧是感染的常见症状。

normal.cn: 债务上升是更深层问题的征兆。

normal.cn: 医生询问了每一个症状。

abstract.en: A symptom is the body telling the truth it cannot say.

abstract.en: Treat the cause, not only the symptom.
abstract.cn: 要治原因，不只治症状。

abstract.en: Every symptom is a small arrow pointing inward.
abstract.cn: 每个症状都是一支指向内部的小箭头。

examples.en: She showed no symptoms at first.

root: 来自希腊语 symptoma（同时发生之事），由 syn（一起）与 piptein（落下）构成。

sensesIntro.en: A symptom is a bodily sign of illness or any sign of a deeper problem.
sensesIntro.cn: symptom 是疾病的体征，也是更深层问题的迹象。

core.en: An outward sign pointing to a hidden cause.
core.cn: 指向隐藏原因的外在迹象。

branches.en: Fever is a common symptom of infection.
branches.cn: 发烧是感染的常见症状。

branches.en: Rising debt is a symptom of deeper trouble.
branches.cn: 债务上升是更深层问题的征兆。

branches.en: Fatigue can be an early symptom.
branches.cn: 疲倦可能是早期症状。

branches.en: The doctor asked about every symptom.
branches.cn: 医生询问了每一个症状。

intro.en: Symptom forms symptoms and the adjectives symptomatic and asymptomatic.
intro.cn: symptom 可构成复数 symptoms 与形容词 symptomatic、asymptomatic。

latinIntro.en: Symptom is Greek; Latin signum, a mark, gives sign and signal.
latinIntro.cn: symptom 源自希腊语；拉丁语 signum（记号）衍生出 sign 与 signal。

definition_en: made by chemical processes rather than taken from nature
core_image: 实验室里的烧瓶被倒出透明纤维，织成一块布
scene: 这件外套用的是合成纤维。This jacket is made of synthetic fibres.
sceneCN: 这里 synthetic 是「合成的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这件外套用的是合成纤维。

senses.title: Made by chemical synthesis
senses.definition: produced by combining substances in a lab
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中由物质组合而成
senses.example: This jacket is made of synthetic fibres.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套用的是合成纤维。
senses.why: The Greek root means putting things together, so a lab-made material is one assembled from parts.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根意为把东西放在一起，因此实验室制造的材料是由部分组装而成。

senses.title: Not genuine in feeling
senses.definition: insincere, as if manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 不真诚的，仿佛人工制造
senses.example: He answered with a synthetic smile.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着假笑回答。
senses.why: If a material can be manufactured, so can an emotion that looks real but is not.
senses.whyCN: 材料可以制造，看起来真实却并非真实的情感也可以。

intro.en: Synthetic comes from Greek synthetikos, skilled at putting together.
intro.cn: synthetic 源自希腊语 synthetikos，意为善于组合。

items.en: Synthesis meant a putting together.
items.cn: synthesis 意为放在一起。

items.en: Tithenai meant to place.
items.cn: tithenai 意为放置。

items.en: Modern Latin syntheticus kept the combining sense.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语 syntheticus 保留组合之义。

items.en: Synthetic entered chemistry for lab-made compounds.
items.cn: synthetic 进入化学领域，指实验室制造的化合物。

items.en: Synthetic widened to anything artificial or insincere.
items.cn: synthetic 扩展到任何人工或虚假之物。

note.en: Synthetic is compared with look-alike words and with words for artificial things.
note.cn: 把 synthetic 与形近词以及表示人造的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Synthetic means assembled by human hands instead of grown by nature.
normalIntro.cn: synthetic 指由人手工合成，而非自然生长。

normal.en: This jacket is made of synthetic fibres.
normal.cn: 这件外套用的是合成纤维。

normal.en: Synthetic rubber replaced natural rubber in tyres.
normal.cn: 合成橡胶在轮胎中取代了天然橡胶。

normal.en: The fabric is cheap because it is synthetic.
normal.cn: 这种布料便宜，因为是合成的。

normal.en: He answered with a synthetic smile.
The drug is synthetic but effective.
normal.cn: 这种药是合成的，但很有效。

abstract.en: Synthetic is nature rewritten in a laboratory hand.
abstract.cn: 合成是用实验室的手重写自然。

abstract.en: What is synthetic can be perfect and still feel wrong.
abstract.cn: 合成的可以完美，却仍让人觉得不对。

abstract.en: We build materials, and sometimes we build our smiles.
abstract.cn: 我们制造材料，有时也制造笑容。

examples.en: This jacket is made of synthetic fibres.
examples.cn: 这件外套用的是合成纤维。

examples.en: Synthetic rubber replaced natural rubber in tyres.
examples.cn: 合成橡胶在轮胎中取代了天然橡胶。

examples.en: He answered with a synthetic smile.

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · syn-（一起）+ thet（放置）+ -ic
dict_mnemonic.text: syn- 表示一起，thet 表示放置，-ic 为形容词词尾；把物质放在一起造出来的，就是「合成的」。

root: 来自希腊语 synthetikos（善于组合），由 syn（一起）与 tithenai（放置）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Synthetic means made by chemical combination, and by extension not genuine.
sensesIntro.cn: synthetic 表示化学合成的，引申为不真诚的。

core.en: Parts assembled by hand into something that looks natural.
core.cn: 各部分被手工组装成看似自然之物。

branches.en: This jacket is made of synthetic fibres.
branches.cn: 这件外套用的是合成纤维。

branches.en: Synthetic rubber replaced natural rubber in tyres.
branches.cn: 合成橡胶在轮胎中取代了天然橡胶。

branches.en: The drug is synthetic but effective.
branches.cn: 这种药是合成的，但很有效。

branches.en: He answered with a synthetic smile.
branches.cn: 他带着假笑回答。

branches.en: What is synthetic can imitate but not belong.
branches.cn: 合成之物能模仿，却无法归属于自然。

intro.en: Synthetic forms synthesis, synthesize and synthetically.
intro.cn: synthetic 可构成 synthesis、synthesize 与 synthetically。

latinIntro.en: Synthetic is Greek; Latin componere, to put together, gives compose.
latinIntro.cn: synthetic 源自希腊语；拉丁语 componere（放在一起）衍生出 compose。

items.example: The essay is a synthesis of ideas.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是各种观点的综合。
这种化合物是人工合成的。

latinEntries.example: Latin componere means to put together.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 componere 意为放在一起。

definition_en: a set of connected parts or rules working together
core_image: 地铁线路图上纵横交错的彩色线条汇成一个网络
scene: 这座城市的地铁系统非常方便。The city s metro system is very convenient.
sceneCN: 这里 system 是「系统」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座城市的地铁系统非常方便。

senses.title: Connected parts working together
senses.definition: a group of parts that operate as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体运作的一组部件
senses.example: The city s metro system is very convenient.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的地铁系统非常方便。
senses.why: The Greek word meant an organized whole, which is exactly the modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词意为有组织的整体，正是现代的含义。

senses.title: An established set of rules
senses.definition: an organized set of rules or customs
senses.definitionCN: 一套有组织的规则或惯例
senses.example: The tax system favours small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 税制对小企业有利。
senses.why: Rules arranged into a working whole are a system in the same sense as machinery.
senses.whyCN: 规则被安排成运作的整体，与机械系统同理。

senses.title: An organized method
senses.definition: a planned way of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 有计划的行事方式
senses.example: She has a system for taking notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一套记笔记的方法。
senses.why: A personal routine can also be an organized whole, so the word covers method.
senses.whyCN: 个人习惯也能构成有组织的整体，因此这个词也指方法。

senses.title: The body as a whole
senses.definition: the body or one of its functional groups
senses.definitionCN: 身体或其中某个功能组
senses.example: Exercise strengthens the immune system.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼增强免疫系统。
senses.why: The body is the most literal set of connected parts, so its groups are also systems.
senses.whyCN: 身体是最字面的相连部件集合，因此其各类功能组也叫系统。

intro.en: System comes from Greek systema, an organized whole.
intro.cn: system 源自希腊语 systema，意为有组织的整体。

items.en: Systema meant a whole put together from parts.
items.cn: systema 意为由部分组成整体。

items.en: Synistanai meant to set up together.
items.cn: synistanai 意为一起建立。

items.en: Late Latin systema named an arranged whole.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 systema 指安排好的整体。

items.en: French systeme carried the ordered sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 systeme 把有序整体的含义带入英语。

items.en: System extended to rules, methods and the body.
items.cn: system 扩展到制度、方法与身体。

note.en: System is compared with look-alike words and with words for organized wholes.
note.cn: 把 system 与形近词以及表示有序整体的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A system is parts plus the connections that make them work.
normalIntro.cn: system 是部件加上让它们运作的连接。

normal.en: The city s metro system is very convenient.
normal.cn: 这座城市的地铁系统非常方便。

normal.en: The tax system favours small firms.
She has a system for taking notes.
normal.cn: 她有一套记笔记的方法。

normal.en: Exercise strengthens the immune system.
The solar system has eight planets.

abstract.en: A system is a promise that parts will take care of each other.
abstract.cn: 系统是部件彼此照应的承诺。

abstract.en: Every system has a blind spot it cannot see.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都有自己看不见的盲点。

abstract.en: We build systems, then systems build our days.
abstract.cn: 我们建造系统，系统又塑造我们的日子。

core.en: Separate parts standing together as one working whole.
core.cn: 分离的部件作为整体一同运作。

definition_zh: 系统的；有条理的；有计划的
definition_en: done according to a fixed plan or method
core_image: 实验台上每份样本都贴着编号标签，按顺序排开
scene: 他们做了一次系统的调查。They carried out a systematic survey.
sceneCN: 这里 systematic 是「系统的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们做了一次系统的调查。

senses.title: Done by a fixed method
senses.definition: following an organized plan rather than chance
senses.definitionCN: 按有组织的计划而非随意进行
senses.example: They carried out a systematic survey.
senses.exampleCN: 他们做了一次系统的调查。
senses.why: The adjective turns system into a way of acting, so it names work done by ordered method.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把系统变成行事方式，因此指按有序方法所做的工作。

senses.title: Regular and orderly in habit
senses.definition: keeping things in a neat, ordered way
senses.definitionCN: 把事物保持整齐有序
senses.example: She is systematic about filing receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 她整理收据很有条理。
senses.why: A person can embody a system too, which gives the sense of orderly habit.
senses.whyCN: 人也能体现系统，于是产生有条理习惯之义。

intro.cn: systematic 建立在希腊语 systema（有组织的整体）之上。

items.en: Systema meant a whole arranged from parts.
items.cn: systema 意为由部分安排成的整体。

items.en: Systematikos meant skilled in arranging.
items.cn: systematikos 意为善于安排。

items.en: Modern Latin systematicus kept the arranging sense.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语 systematicus 保留安排之义。

items.en: Systematic described work done by method.
items.cn: systematic 描述按方法进行的工作。

items.en: Systematic extended to orderly personal habits.
items.cn: systematic 扩展到有条理的个人习惯。

note.en: Systematic is compared with look-alike words and with words for orderly work.

normalIntro.en: Systematic means letting a plan, not mood, decide the next step.
normalIntro.cn: systematic 指让计划而非心情决定下一步。

normal.en: They carried out a systematic survey.
normal.cn: 他们做了一次系统的调查。

normal.en: She is systematic about filing receipts.
The team made a systematic search of the archive.
normal.cn: 团队对档案做了系统搜索。

normal.en: His training was slow but systematic.
normal.cn: 他的训练缓慢但有系统。

normal.en: A systematic error repeats in the same direction.
normal.cn: 系统误差总是朝同一方向重复。

abstract.en: Systematic work is patience made visible.
abstract.cn: 系统的工作是看得见的耐心。

abstract.en: Chance favours the systematic mind.
abstract.cn: 机会偏爱有条理的头脑。

abstract.en: To be systematic is to trust the next step more than the mood.
abstract.cn: 有条理就是更相信下一步，而不是此刻的心情。

examples.en: They carried out a systematic survey.

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · system + -atic
dict_mnemonic.text: system 是系统，加形容词词尾 -atic 成为 systematic，表示「按系统进行的」，即有系统、有条理。

root: 来自希腊语 systematikos（善于安排的），由 systema（有组织的整体）派生。

sensesIntro.en: Systematic means done by ordered method, or keeping things orderly by habit.
sensesIntro.cn: systematic 表示按有序方法进行，或习惯上保持整齐。

core.en: A plan applied step by step without skipping.
core.cn: 一个逐步执行、不跳步的计划。

branches.en: They carried out a systematic survey.
branches.cn: 他们做了一次系统的调查。

branches.en: The team made a systematic search of the archive.
branches.cn: 团队对档案做了系统搜索。

branches.en: She is systematic about filing receipts.
branches.cn: 她整理收据很有条理。

branches.en: A systematic error repeats in the same direction.
branches.cn: 系统误差总是朝同一方向重复。

branches.en: His training was slow but systematic.
branches.cn: 他的训练缓慢但有系统。

intro.en: Systematic forms systematically and relates to system and systematize.

latinIntro.en: Systematic is Greek; Latin methodus, a way of pursuit, gives method.

items.example: He is methodical in his work.

latinEntries.example: Latin methodus means a way of pursuit.

definition_zh: 有系统的；有体系的；按部就班的
definition_en: arranged or carried out according to a system
core_image: 档案柜的抽屉依次拉开，每格都贴着同样的标签格式
scene: 他的整理方式很有系统。His filing method was systematical.
sceneCN: 这里 systematical 是「有系统的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的整理方式很有系统。

senses.title: Arranged as a system
senses.definition: laid out as a connected whole
senses.definitionCN: 按相连整体来安排
senses.example: His filing method was systematical.
senses.exampleCN: 他的整理方式很有系统。
senses.why: This longer form adds -al to systematic, stressing the state of being arranged as a system.
senses.whyCN: 这个较长形式在 systematic 后加 -al，强调被安排成系统的状态。

senses.title: Following set steps
senses.definition: carried out step by step in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序一步步进行
senses.example: The training was systematical from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 训练从第一天起就按部就班。
senses.why: A system imposes an order of steps, which yields the sense of doing things in sequence.
senses.whyCN: 系统规定了步骤次序，于是产生按部就班之义。

intro.en: Systematical adds the adjective ending -al to systematic.
intro.cn: systematical 是在 systematic 后加形容词词尾 -al 而成。

items.en: Systema meant an organized whole.
items.cn: systema 意为有组织的整体。

items.en: Systematikos meant skilled in arranging.
items.cn: systematikos 意为善于安排。

items.en: Systematic entered English as ordered by method.
items.cn: systematic 以「按方法有序」之义进入英语。

items.en: Systematical added -al to stress the arranged state.
items.cn: systematical 加 -al 以强调被安排的状态。

items.en: Systematical survives mainly as a rarer variant.
items.cn: systematical 主要作为较少见的变体留存。

note.en: Systematical is compared with look-alike words and with words for ordered arrangement.
note.cn: 把 systematical 与形近词以及表示有序安排的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Systematical describes things that have been given a system.
normalIntro.cn: systematical 描述已被赋予系统的事物。

normal.en: His filing method was systematical.
normal.cn: 他的整理方式很有系统。

normal.en: The training was systematical from the first day.
normal.cn: 训练从第一天起就按部就班。

normal.en: She kept a systematical record of every lesson.
normal.cn: 她为每节课做系统记录。

normal.en: The course offers a systematical study of grammar.
normal.cn: 这门课提供系统的语法学习。

normal.en: Their approach was systematical rather than random.
normal.cn: 他们的方法有系统，而非随意。

abstract.en: Systematical is order made into a habit.
abstract.cn: 有系统就是把秩序变成习惯。

abstract.en: A systematical mind leaves nothing to chance.
abstract.cn: 有系统的头脑不把任何事交给偶然。

abstract.en: Structure outside calms the noise inside.
abstract.cn: 外在的结构能平息内在的嘈杂。

root: 由 systematic 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，最终源自希腊语 systema（有组织的整体）。

sensesIntro.en: Systematical means arranged as a system, or carried out step by step.
sensesIntro.cn: systematical 表示按系统安排，或一步步执行。

core.en: Order that has been built into the way things are kept.
core.cn: 秩序已被建入事物的存放方式。

branches.en: His filing method was systematical.
branches.cn: 他的整理方式很有系统。

branches.en: She kept a systematical record of every lesson.
branches.cn: 她为每节课做系统记录。

branches.en: The training was systematical from the first day.

intro.en: Systematical forms systematically and is a variant of systematic.
intro.cn: systematical 可构成 systematically，是 systematic 的变体。

latinIntro.en: The -al ending is Latin; Latin ordo, order, underlies the meaning.
latinIntro.cn: -al 词尾源自拉丁语；其含义根植于拉丁语 ordo（次序）。

definition_zh: 桌子；表格；一桌人；提交（议案）
definition_en: a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs, or an arranged set of facts
core_image: 木桌中央摆着茶壶，四条桌腿稳稳压住地板
scene: 晚饭已经摆在桌上了。Dinner is already on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 table 是「桌子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：晚饭已经摆在桌上了。

senses.title: A piece of furniture
senses.definition: furniture with a flat top and legs
senses.definitionCN: 有平面与支腿的家具
senses.example: Dinner is already on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭已经摆在桌上了。
senses.why: The Latin word tabula named a flat board, which is exactly the object we still call a table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 tabula 指平板，正是我们今天仍称作桌子的物件。

senses.title: Facts set out in rows
senses.definition: facts arranged in rows and columns
senses.definitionCN: 按行列排列的事实
senses.example: The results are shown in the table below.
senses.exampleCN: 结果见下表。
senses.why: A flat board is where figures were laid out, so an arranged set of facts kept the same name.
senses.whyCN: 平板是摆放数字的地方，因此按规则排列的事实沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: The people seated together
senses.definition: a group of people sitting at one table
senses.definitionCN: 围坐一桌的一群人
senses.example: The whole table laughed at the story.
senses.exampleCN: 一桌人都被这个故事逗笑了。
senses.why: The furniture stands for the group gathered around it, a common kind of transfer.
senses.whyCN: 家具代指围坐其旁的人群，这是常见的转喻。

senses.title: To present formally
senses.definition: to propose something for discussion
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出供讨论
senses.example: They tabled a motion at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在会上提交了一项动议。
senses.why: A document placed on the table is offered to the assembly, so the noun became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 把文件放到桌上就是提交给会议，于是名词转为动词。

intro.en: Table comes from Latin tabula, a flat board or writing tablet.
intro.cn: table 源自拉丁语 tabula，指平板或书写板。

items.en: Tabula meant a board, plank or writing tablet.
items.cn: tabula 指板、木板或书写板。

items.en: Table named a board and then a table.
items.cn: table 先指木板，后指桌子。

items.en: Table covered furniture and written lists.
items.cn: table 兼指家具与书面清单。

items.en: Table became a verb meaning to present formally.
items.cn: table 转为动词，表示正式提交。

items.en: Table also names a group seated together.
items.cn: table 也指围坐一桌的一群人。

note.en: Table is compared with look-alike words and with other furniture and lists.
note.cn: 把 table 与形近词以及其他家具与清单类词作比较。
